summary: Division of Forestry tower built 1950 near Dennison, 80 feet tall, watched by Joe Eslick until 1967; described in 2018 as standing, abandoned and in disrepair.

facts.design: About 80 feet tall, with 107 steps to the top; a telephone and two-way radio were installed
facts.status_note: A 2018 Times-Reporter article describes it as still standing, abandoned and in a state of disrepair; no newer report was found.
facts.agency: Ohio Department of Natural Resources (Division of Forestry)

events.note: Built by the Division of Forestry; the 1967 clipping calls 1950 the year of its erection
Went into operation in 1951; Joe Eslick became watchman that year
Watchman Joe Eslick retired at age 70; the article does not say who watched after him
Division-wide date: the Division of Forestry stopped using its towers as fire lookouts in 1978; Tappan's own end date is not given
FFLA Ohio chapter report: one of two state-owned towers in need of painting
Date registered September 3, 2014 as US 1029, OH 17
Times-Reporter: still standing, abandoned and in a state of disrepair

notes_for_editor: Read: NHLR Tappan page; Times-Reporter 2018 article (live page returned 403, Internet Archive copy used and quoted from); Eastern lookouts Tappan page (1967 clipping and ODNR header); FFLA Ohio 2010 chapter report; FFLA Ohio list. Build year 1950 is consistent across sources (the article adds 1951 as the year of operation, which is not a conflict). The 1978 end date is given for the Division's towers as a whole; the article does not say when Tappan's own watch ended. The article says most towers were sold or removed but does not say whether Tappan was one of the seven the Division kept; the 2010 report calls Tappan state-owned. No source gives access, visiting or climbing information, so no access level is recorded. Newest condition report is 2018. Not read: the Find a Grave page for Joe Eslick.
